rv.q: Just the dishevelled beauty of a self-contained omnishambles, a Schadenfreude nightmare brought to life by the sheer force of human incompetence.
It calls for acting larger-than-life and inch-perfect. It gets it.
Frayn's ingenious farce-within-a-farce sees a clunky touring production of a faded bedroom farce, Nothing On, fall apart around the performers' ears.
Noises Off is classic farce, very well constructed, and as complex and silly as you would expect. It also, by default, feels quite dated.
Jeremy Herrin’s superb revival has tightened up further for this encore run, resulting in the funniest night you’ll have in the West End.
Noises Off is a feat of extraordinary timing, character development and chaos with ensuing hilarity.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this West End revival as a masterclass in farce, praising its sublime chaos, extraordinary timing, and inch-perfect performances that make Frayn's ingenious meta-theatrical comedy feel effortlessly hilarious.

vr.q: I give noises off at the Garrick Theatre five stars
